reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is the matched-uncertainty adaptive control law, which extends classical linear-in-parameters control to nonparametric RKHS settings. It uses a kernel integral operator to represent the unknown dynamics h(x) as a function of past inputs, enabling adaptive updates even in infinite dimensions. The key innovation lies in the randomized kernel approximation using random Fourier features, which allows finite-dimensional implementation with explicit bounds on prediction error. This is achieved through the kernel trick (Observation 4.1) and Theorem 6.4/6.7, which show that the tracking error converges to a ball of size B_approx. The gradient flow reinterpretation (7.3) connects this to optimization dynamics, offering empirical expressiveness but sacrificing formal stability guarantees. The dual nature of this framework—adaptive control and state estimation—is captured by the LQR/Kalman-like duality mentioned in the appendix. The failure mode occurs when the assumptions on h(x) or feature maps are violated, leading to loss of convergence or instability.
